ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: image1 shows the shape that is forbidden to appear: a 2×2 square composed of 4 small squares, and these 4 small squares are all colored gray. The chessboard in image2 is a centered diamond composed of small squares; counting the number of small squares row by row gives 1, 3, 5, 7, 5, 3, 1, so there are a total of 1+3+5+7+5+3+1=25 small squares. Then reason: In order for the gray 2×2 block in image1 not to appear, every possible 2×2 small block must have at least 1 small square not colored gray. That is to say, we can transform it into: at least how many small squares not colored gray must be left so that they can cover all possible 2×2 blocks. First give the upper bound: In this diamond chessboard, 4 pairwise non-overlapping 2×2 blocks can be found, for example respectively located in the upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, and lower-right regions. Because these 4 2×2 blocks do not overlap with one another, and each one needs at least 1 small square not colored gray, at least 4 small squares not colored gray must be left. Therefore at most 25-4=21 small squares can be colored gray. Then explain that 21 can be achieved: View the diamond as 7 rows with row lengths 1, 3, 5, 7, 5, 3, 1. In the 3rd row, leave the 2nd and 4th small squares not colored gray, and in the 5th row also leave the corresponding 2nd and 4th small squares not colored gray; color all the remaining 21 small squares gray. Check the possible 2×2 blocks: between rows 1 and 2 and between rows 6 and 7, a 2×2 cannot be formed; every 2×2 between rows 2 and 3 is blocked by the blank squares left in row 3; between rows 3 and 4 it is also blocked by these two blank squares in row 3; between rows 4 and 5 it is blocked by the two blank squares in row 5; between rows 5 and 6 it is also blocked by the two blank squares in row 5. Therefore a 2×2 block composed of 4 small gray squares will not appear. So at most 21 small squares can be colored gray.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: image1 illustrates the forbidden pattern, namely a 2-by-2 block of four grey small squares. In image2, read the board as a centered diamond of grid squares with row lengths 1, 3, 5, 7, 5, 3, 1, so there are 25 small squares total. Convert the task into choosing some squares to leave unpainted so that every possible 2-by-2 block in the diamond contains at least one unpainted square. For the upper bound, identify four pairwise disjoint 2-by-2 blocks in the diamond, for example one near the upper-left part, one near the upper-right part, one near the lower-left part, and one near the lower-right part. Since these four forbidden blocks are disjoint, at least one square in each must be left unpainted, so at least 4 squares are unpainted and at most 25 - 4 = 21 squares can be grey. For achievability, exhibit four unpainted squares that hit every possible 2-by-2 block, such as the two separated interior squares in the third row and the corresponding two separated interior squares in the fifth row; then check row-pair by row-pair that every 2-by-2 block contains one of these four blanks. Thus 21 grey squares are possible and maximal.
